concepts.summary: Schema validator/mutator for INTENT.md and LEDGER.md (INTENT-mode planning contract + BFS realization trail), plus TASKS.md/SESSION.md query helpers used by /z-execute and the context curator.

Lockless per-run JSON registry (under the external artifact base) that lets concurrent z-harness sessions discover each other's plans, seed likely file scope via a Haiku scope-extractor, and advisorily coordinate via a per-file claim/release/wait-for lease mechanism; overlap is always advisory except one strict-mode hard gate.

Specialized subagent prompt files under agents/: each is spawned fresh per invocation, executes an isolated worker role (implementation, review, planning-route advice, doc sync, mechanical remote/bisect/lookup work, cross-LLM consult), and returns a parseable contract that the surrounding /z-* commands parse and act on.

Advisory behavioral-rule layer mined from interaction history, stored two-layer (global+project), compiled into KERNEL.md; store/resolver/kernel machinery is fully live, but all five /z-axiom-* commands are currently broken self-referential stubs.

Per-host adapter/export/command-tier capability matrix (claude/omp/antigravity/cursor/codex adapters + windsurf/kiro/cline/copilot/pi export-only hosts), gated for OMP and Codex by dedicated parity gates that read T008/Codex parity test evidence at call time.

Slash-command contract catalogue covering explicit routing, z-plan's single-gate prose plan-brief + known-work DAG (work-graph.json), z-execute's INTENT-mode acceptance-evaluator/divergence-halt scheduler and native model routing, z-brainstorm/z-sharpen pre-planning, Hermes-marker integration (handoff/fanout/needs_input), and docs maintenance through doc-updater rather than ad hoc index edits.

Read-only work-thread recovery for fuzzy or exact prior-work targets. /z-resume selects a bounded plan/run/worktree/branch/artifact/repo target, reports evidence-backed state and ambiguity, recommends safe continuations without executing them, and delegates --report to /z-report only after selection.

Unified z-harness configuration system: 4-layer TOML config loader (Loader API) plus the workflow question-registry/resolver/writer built on top of it (Workflow Resolver), including model-class routing.
LLM-free pre-run token-cost estimator + gate helper + subagent cost model gating seven expensive z-harness skills via one profile file and one cost_gate_decision event.
Read-only Haiku lookup worker that fetches external docs/APIs and returns bounded STATUS-headed syntheses.

Durable follow-up registry draining out-of-scope discoveries into a priority-ordered lifecycle-tracked work queue. Three sinks (project, global, Notion mirror); conservative open->running->verify->done state machine; three completion paths (human-confirmed, audit-confirmed, auto-closed-low-risk). Shared module followup_common.py centralizes the two-tier lock model (per-entry + global cross-tool flock with .hb.lock-serialized holder JSON), batched config reads, and backgrounded Notion push. Event-sourced index.jsonl with incremental checkpoint rebuild (T010), compaction to index.archive.jsonl, corruption detection/repair, and materialized notion_sync_pending state.
Canonical STATUS-headed Markdown contract used by external-lookup results, including provenance, budget, freshness, and refusal semantics.

Target-specific export pipeline. OMP export is native for its explicit .omp/z-harness package layout. Codex export fidelity is partial: it emits native skills, custom-agent TOML under .codex/agents/, .codex-plugin/plugin.json, AGENTS.md fallback/reference, mcp_config.json, runtime scripts, and persona prompts via the adapter persona loop, while Codex adapter/runtime command orchestration remains degraded for ordinary commands and blocked for native multi-agent command families unless Codex parity evidence, runtime primitive evidence, and a CodexDriver native hook exist.

/z-overnight runs a linear chain of z-harness sub-commands unattended, converting instrumented AskUserQuestion callsites to halt events under Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt, writing MORNING_REPORT.md and push-notifying at every terminal transition.

TOML-bound persona/model/runtime resolution + a boring-anchor/no-persona rotation experiment (default ON) across implementer/reviewer/consultant/ideator/audit_persona roles, with per-target export adapters for Antigravity/Cursor/Codex/Claude.

pi (pi.dev) is an export-only compatibility target: runtime/drivers/pi/export.py renders z-harness agents/skills as pi agent/prompt files, copies vendored pi-only assets and deterministic /z-resume runtime scripts, and applies four layers of YAML frontmatter defense; no adapter/HostDriver exists, unlike OMP's native T009 support.

Slug-level hard flock claim lock (plan-claim.sh over sink-lock.sh) that prevents two Claude sessions from double-working the same /z-plan or /z-audit-plan slug; orthogonal to the advisory active-plan-registry.
External artifact-base resolution (5-tier fallback + anchor split-brain guard) for all z-harness plan/telemetry paths, plus the safe copy-verify-rm migrator from legacy in-repo layouts.

Runtime provider registry (.z-harness/providers.json) resolving consultant/reviewer roles to CLI invocation descriptors, layered under a TOML role-runtime override axis with legacy [models]/providers.json.roles fallbacks, alias resolution, and per-dispatch auth/PATH preflight.

Haiku subagent (agents/review-agent.md) + scripts/run-memory-review.sh helper that proposes 0-3 memory candidates after /z-execute, /z-review-all, or /z-debug; the post-agent review loop and write-through behavior differ by parent_command (z-execute has no interactive accept loop; z-review-all and z-debug do).

Unified Run Brief receipt (archive/$RUN/run-brief.json) emitted at finalize by 9 registry commands; render-run-brief.py renders chat/push text from it; /z-do is now a deprecated pass-through alias to /z-plan --quick and no longer independently participates.

Operational utility scripts: structured telemetry (log-event.sh/log-phase.sh), layered TOML config + model routing (config.py/config.sh), the lockless active-plan registry with F1-F5 cross-session lease/wait/claim primitives (active-plan-registry.py), the git-safety PreToolUse hook (block-dangerous-git.sh), memory/dismissal maintenance scripts, remote sandbox sync, and persona-rotation analysis.

Durable SESSION.md context handoff for /z-execute: notable-only breadcrumbs (E2) feed a Haiku context-curator (E3) that folds them into a bounded SESSION.md at clear checkpoints, which E1 re-inlines on resume via a shared done_ids_hash; write-handoff.sh (now fronted by the cross-command write-clear-checkpoint.sh) emits the machine-readable handoff.json continuation token.

z-harness configuration cockpit: public z-harness setup CLI (harness detection via release_surface + posture apply) plus the in-harness /z-setup skill/scripts/setup.py (inspect, wizard, apply, explain, status) which is the sole writer of config.py-managed state.
Fast lightweight bug-fix command for known-diagnosis cases: bundled two-LLM light-fix consult, inline implementation, mandatory Codex review, single FIX.md artifact, ~15 min target.

Reusable bounded idea-sharpening component plus /z-sharpen wrapper. The component assesses clarity and alternatives, returns proceed/sharpen_more/route_to_brainstorm plus GRILL.md content when ready; the wrapper owns slug, collision, telemetry, final write, and advisory handoff. /z-plan now invokes the component as a mandatory pre-Premise-check step (0-sharpen).

Cheap opt-in pre-planning ideation: Phase 0 reuses the shared z-sharpen component when GRILL.md is absent, then parses ideator count, probes scope, dispatches ideators, writes BRAINSTORM.md, and waits for user discussion/lock-in without auto-dispatching /z-plan.
Read-only Haiku agent that clusters wide-mode ideator framings by core approach axis and reports effective diversity without selecting a winner.

Deterministic z-harness update path: a thin /z-update host skill delegates all release-manifest fetch, version comparison, and install-mode dispatch to z_harness_cli/commands/update.py + release.py, with install.sh owning the actual symlink/tarball plugin install and atomic-swap mechanics.

Bulk codebase quality uplift: decomposes a repo into components, runs a cross-cutting pass plus per-component correctness/cleanliness/design audits, and drives sequential /z-execute implementation behind resumable MANIFEST-tracked AskUser gates.

Machine-readable session-continuity contract (handoff.json, JSON Schema draft 2020-12) letting any z-harness agent (pi, Claude Code, Codex CLI) hand off to a fresh session: protocol 1.0 (7 fields) or 1.1 (adds attend_resume predicate for /z-attend yields). Producer-side is skills/z-handoff/SKILL.md (interactive) and scripts/write-handoff.sh (automated, wraps write-clear-checkpoint.sh); consumers are Hermes, /z-attend, and session-orchestration watchers.
Mechanical per-task docs sync agent that stages AUTO-section and LLM machine-field updates from task diffs for later reconciliation.
Narrative documentation command and accumulator for finalized tier2-context.json, generating ADRs, rationale, migration guides, and concept doc cross-links.
Canonical optional registry of stable repo-specific behavioral invariants (docs/INVARIANTS.json) consumed by /z-test, /z-execute, /z-review-all, and adaptive INTENT.

Shared Codex final-message capture pattern (-o outfile probe/fallback) plus review/consult telemetry and contracts shared by agents/reviewer.md, agents/consultant-primary.md, and agents/consultant-secondary.md.
Non-blocking per-subagent-dispatch cost telemetry: host detection, host-stamped event logging, and the retrospective subagent-costs read-side pricer for /z-stats.

Opt-in Flash/Haiku pre-review layer: per-task /z-execute gate-down via runtime.impl_pre_review (skips codex on eligible low-tier CLEAN verdicts) plus the shared pre-reviewer/complexity-classifier subagents; both gate-down and the sibling runtime.pre_review context-prep cycles (z-review-all, z-audit-plan) default off and fail safe toward full reviewer coverage.

Attended middle-gear chain runner: auto-answers mechanical gates, surfaces decision/risk/shortcut/archiving gates inline, and yields with protocol-1.1 handoff predicates at plan and implement-all boundaries.

Dormant-by-default Hermes parallel execution layer: generates workstream DAGs, runs conflict-safe workstreams in isolated git worktrees, serializes merges, and can schedule conflict-free plans under sorted plan-claim locks when workflow.hermes_enabled is explicitly true.

Default /z-plan intent-compiler and adaptive INTENT execution model: /z-plan compiles conversation into INTENT.md plus an initial append-only known-work graph (work-graph.json), and /z-execute freezes INTENT then schedules over that graph via task-tree-generator (now a known-work graph expander) with LEDGER checkpoints and durable-DAG-settle-point acceptance evaluation.

Shared amendment-continuation helpers: amend-gate-decision maps workflow.audit_to_amend resolver envelopes to auto_split/force_ask/halt for z-audit-plan Phase 5, and amendment-brief renders spec_gap corrections plus premise_failure concerns for z-audit-plan and z-review-all; z-review-all's own Phase 6.5 auto-amend is severity-agnostic and does not consult the gate decision.

Read-only, claim-first, contract-level pre-implementation plan audit: low-risk plans skip via a fast-path; otherwise reality-check + design audit + optional pre-review + adversarial cross-LLM review feed a Class-tagged (spec_gap|premise_failure) PLAN_AUDIT_REPORT.md, then Phase 5 auto-amends spec_gap findings via /z-amend and surfaces premise_failure concerns as a prose brief, with a Phase 9 preference-elevation proposal.

Final cross-LLM plan review over cumulative diff: promotes drift/spec-gap findings into REVIEW-TASKS, auto-amends amendment proposals, renders amendment brief/run-brief, finalizes tier2 context, and then runs memory review.

Read-mostly workspace consistency audit joining worktrees, plan artifacts, active-plan registry records, claim locks, uncommitted work, and follow-up opportunities; cleanup is opt-in per flag with per-item confirmation.

Two-layer liveness protection: supervised-run.sh enforces hard process-group deadlines for killable subprocesses (confirmed active in production telemetry); schedule-hang-check.sh/hang-check.sh schedule a metrics-derived one-shot stall detector for native-agent stalls that has never been observed to fire outside tests.
